messages:
aj: Noticing a spike in SSE reconnects for a subset of tenants after last night's route change. Clients hit 409s and go into tight reconnect loops. Anyone else seeing this in telemetry?

maria: Yup saw ~2% of live sessions show repeated 'resume failed: route-mismatch' in logs. Looks correlated with sticky-routing swaps during canary.

ben: Quota billing is weird too — those reconnect attempts are counted as full new sessions so customers see token+session charges.

jess: Repro steps I ran: 1) open SSE to model A on route r1 2) redeploy and rip route to r2 3) client tries resume with old session id -> 409 -> client reopens and server issues new session id.

samir: Root cause guess: resume id includes route fingerprint, so when our routing policy atomically switches sticky lease, the server rejects resume. Missing telemetry tag for "route_before" and "route_after" makes console attribution hard.

aj: Proposed fixes: (a) make resume idempotent across compatible route variants (route-agnostic resume token) OR (b) on route flip, emit a grace mapping that accepts resumes for X seconds. Also need to stop counting failed resumes as billable new sessions.

maria: (b) seems lower risk short-term. We can add server-side mapping to accept resume tokens for 30s after route flips and backfill metrics. But then we need console changes to show which route served the resumed session.

ben: For billing, we can mark those resumed requests with "resume_retry=true" metric and exclude from session-creation meter until final handshake succeeds. That requires metering change + retroactive dashboard correction.

jess: Small patch I sketched for client backoff to avoid tight loops:
```
let retry = 0;
while (retry < 6) {
  await sleep(min(250 * 2**retry, 5000));
  tryResume();
  retry++;
}
```
Add jitter and only escalate to full re-auth after N failed resumes.

samir: We also need to update the rollout UX in Console: add a "route flip safety" toggle that keeps route-compatible variants grouped and enables the 30s resume window during canary. Without UI, teams keep flipping and see customer impact.

aj: Action items: Maria + Ben implement 30s resume mapping + metric tag (resume_retry) and exclude from billing meter; Jess add jittered client backoff and bump SDK patch; Samir + Product add Console toggle and per-session route timeline in the live-sessions view; I'll own rollout plan and canary policy.

maria: ETA: hotfix PR today, smoke in staging tomorrow.

ben: I'll change metering and add a migration job to correct last 6h of billing for affected tenants.

jess: SDK PR ready in draft, needs API sign-off for new error codes.

samir: Console mockups incoming, but for telemetry we should emit both route_before and route_after tags so dashboards can show flips.

deploy-bot: canary started: streaming-router v2 -> 1% traffic at 2026-03-20T14:12:10Z

aj: Hold canary until hotfix lands in router. If we flip again without mapping, we'll see repeated customer noise.

console-bot: NOTE: created ticket PLT-4829 to add "route flip safety" toggle and new live-sessions column.

ben: Last question — do we treat resumed sessions that later fully re-auth as billable only once? I think yes, but we need clear audit trails.

aj: Yes — bill once. Metric hack + audit log for session-id transitions will be sufficient. We'll coordinate with finance to correct invoices if needed.

maria: I'll post updates here when hotfix deployed. For now, please avoid manual route swaps for live tenants. :pray:
